candidates.attacker_control: The raw HTTP request-target path is fully attacker-controlled (method GET/HEAD/POST, no authentication required). The parser accepts literal '.' and '..' segments and rejects only CR/LF/space/tab in the path, so a client can send, for example, GET /./WEB-INF/web.xml or GET /existing/../secret-constraint-file directly. Percent-encoded slashes (%2F/%5C) are re-encoded when ALLOW_ENCODED_SLASH is false and are therefore not needed.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Checked and rejected obvious mitigations: (a) CanonicalPathHandler exists and would canonicalize, but DeploymentManagerImpl's default chain (lines 207-214) does not install it and no other canonicalization call exists in the request pipeline (only ServletContextImpl.getRealPath, HttpServletResponseImpl.sendRedirect, AsyncContextImpl dispatch and HttpServletRequestImpl.getRequestDispatcher canonicalize); (b) URLUtils.decode re-encodes decoded '/' and '\\' when ALLOW_ENCODED_SLASH is false, so %2F/%5C variants are not usable, but literal '.'/'..' segments are unaffected; (c) DefaultServlet.isAllowed blocks paths that start with '/META-INF' or '/WEB-INF' and ServletInitialHandler.isForbiddenPath blocks '/web-inf/...' prefixes, but both are prefix-only checks defeated by a preceding './' or 'x/../' segment; (d) FileResourceManager does perform a canonical-file check, but it only compares the last name component (case-insensitive-filesystem guard) and never verifies containment under base; (e) ServletSecurityConstraintHandler does call the constraint matcher, but with the same un-normalized relativePath, so both the mapping and the constraint check are bypassed consistently.
candidates.impact: Unauthenticated information disclosure and authorization bypass: reading deployment descriptor and class/config files under WEB-INF and META-INF (e.g. web.xml), and reading/serving static files mapped to security-constraint-protected URL patterns without authenticating or satisfying the required roles; the same root cause in core ResourceHandler/FileResourceManager permits escaping the configured file-serving base directory. Scope is any servlet deployment (or standalone resource handler) that does not manually insert the optional CanonicalPathHandler.
candidates.prerequisites: A servlet deployment whose DeploymentInfo uses a FileResourceManager (the normal production configuration for exploded web archives; DefaultServlet reads deployment.getDeploymentInfo().getResourceManager()). A target that exists under the web root (WEB-INF/META-INF content, or a static resource covered by a security-constraint such as /secure/*). No CanonicalPathHandler in front of the deployment chain (DeploymentManagerImpl.deploy() lines 207-214 only install HttpContinueReadHandler and, if configured, URLDecodingHandler). The core ResourceHandler/FileResourceManager variant additionally requires the resource handler to be used for file serving (e.g. examples/filesserving/FileServer uses it without canonicalization).
candidates.root_cause: Untrusted request paths are treated as already-canonical after URL decoding. HttpRequestParser.handlePath (core/.../protocol/http/HttpRequestParser.java:337-399, plus beginQueryParameters/beginPathParameters/handleFullUrl) copies the decoded path verbatim into HttpServerExchange.requestPath/relativePath; no dot-segment normalization occurs anywhere in the request pipeline (only CanonicalPathHandler, an optional handler not installed by DeploymentManagerImpl.deploy(), performs CanonicalPathUtils.canonicalize). All downstream consumers therefore operate on a non-canonical string: (1) ServletInitialHandler.handleRequest uses exchange.getRelativePath() for isForbiddenPath and for servlet mapping; isForbiddenPath only blocks the exact path '/meta-inf/' or a leading '/web-inf/', so '/./WEB-INF/...' or '/x/../WEB-INF/...' passes; (2) DefaultServlet.doGet derives its path from getServletPath()/getPathInfo() and isAllowed() only tests leading '/META-INF'/'/WEB-INF' prefixes and file extensions, so the same path is allowed and handed to the ResourceManager; (3) FileResourceManager.getResource builds new File(base, path) with '..'/'.' still present and only compares file.getCanonicalFile().getName() with file.getName() (a case check on the last component), which does not confine the resolved file to base; (4) ResourceHandler.serveResource uses exchange.getRelativePath() directly for the same lookup; (5) ServletSecurityConstraintHandler evaluates SecurityPathMatches.getSecurityInfo(exchange.getRelativePath(), method), so a constraint registered for e.g. '/secure/*' (prefix key '/secure') does not match '/x/../secure/y', while the default servlet can still resolve and serve base/secure/y.
candidates.title: Request path is never canonicalized before servlet routing, security-constraint checks and filesystem resource resolution (path traversal / reserved-path and constraint bypass)
candidates.trace: GET /./WEB-INF/web.xml -> HttpRequestParser.handlePath stores decoded path '/./WEB-INF/web.xml' into exchange.relativePath (HttpRequestParser.java:349-356) -> ServletInitialHandler.handleRequest: isForbiddenPath('/./WEB-INF/web.xml') is false because the string does not start with '/web-inf/' (ServletInitialHandler.java:103-107,164-167) -> ServletPathMatchesData.getServletHandlerByPath walks back to the always-present default prefix '' and returns ServletPathMatch(defaultServlet, fullPath) so getServletPath() == '/./WEB-INF/web.xml' -> DefaultServlet.doGet -> getPath(req) returns that string and isAllowed() accepts it (no leading /WEB-INF, .xml is allowed) -> FileResourceManager.getResource strips the leading slash, builds new File(base, './WEB-INF/web.xml'), file.exists() is true and file.getCanonicalFile().getName() ('web.xml') equals file.getName(), so the FileResource is returned and served. Analogously '/x/../secure/y' is evaluated by ServletSecurityConstraintHandler via SecurityPathMatches.getSecurityInfo on the un-normalized string, so a '/secure/*' constraint does not apply, while the default servlet still resolves base/secure/y. ResourceHandler does the same lookup with exchange.getRelativePath(), so '/../file' resolves against the parent of the configured base.
candidates.unverified: Not runtime-confirmed: OS-level path resolution, deployment resource-manager configuration and the exact behavior of File.exists() for the crafted paths were reasoned from source (no code was executed). I could not diff this snapshot against the upstream fix commit or the CVE/fix for this case, so I cannot prove this exact behavior was the introduced/regressed change rather than a long-standing upstream weakness; if the deployment inserts a CanonicalPathHandler or normalizes paths upstream (proxy/container), the attack path is blocked. The P1 relation index proves only syntactic call edges (e.g. ServletSecurityConstraintHandler -> SecurityPathMatches.getSecurityInfo), not data flow or reachability.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-22 Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal'); secondary CWE-863 Incorrect Authorization

coverage_summary: Source scope: 595 files (582 Java, plus POMs, one HTML example, resources); 0 files excluded by the safety filters (no binaries, symlinks, or oversized files); snapshot contains no src/test sources, so no tests were available to confirm intended behavior. P1 index: complete for all 595 files, 0 parse errors, 9,851 symbols and 17,324 syntactic edges, but control/data flow and semantic resolution are not implemented and 12,767 calls are unresolved; index facts are navigation hints only (security_call / config_file). I read and reasoned over: the HTTP request pipeline (HttpRequestParser, HttpReadListener, HttpTransferEncoding, HttpServerConnection, HttpContinue), servlet mapping and security wiring (ServletInitialHandler, ServletPathMatches(Data), SecurityPathMatches, ServletSecurityConstraintHandler/RoleHandler, DeploymentManagerImpl, DefaultServlet), resource handling (ResourceHandler, FileResourceManager, FileResource, ClassPathResourceManager, DirectoryUtils), core auth/security mechanisms (Basic/Digest/Form/ClientCert/External/SSO/CachedAuthenticatedSession, SecurityContextImpl, SimpleNonceManager, confidentiality handlers, IPAddressAccessControlHandler, SSLHeaderHandler, JDBC/access-log handlers), session handling (InMemorySessionManager, SecureRandomSessionIdGenerator, session cookie configs), and representative WebSocket handshake/channel code. Uninspected in depth: most of websockets-jsr (AnnotatedEndpoint/FrameHandler/ServerWebSocketContainer), client AJP/HTTP parsers, cache/encoding handlers, ProxyHandler/LoadBalancingProxyClient internals, and several large servlet spec classes (AsyncContextImpl, ServletOutputStreamImpl) beyond targeted spot checks; conclusions about those areas would require further reading.
limitations: No code was executed, compiled, or tested; OS path resolution and deployment wiring behavior were reasoned from source only.

No diff against the upstream repository/fix commit was possible, so it cannot be proven that the missing canonicalization is the regression associated with this case rather than a pre-existing upstream weakness (the framework documents CanonicalPathHandler as opt-in and ResourceManager.getResource as requiring a canonicalized path).
The P1 relation index has no control-flow, data-flow or semantic resolution; all call edges cited are syntactic candidates verified against source text, not runtime facts.
The repository contains no tests, so intended security behavior (e.g. whether deployments are expected to insert CanonicalPathHandler) could not be confirmed from test expectations.
Coverage of websockets-jsr, the HTTP/AJP client parsers, proxy handlers and parts of the servlet spec API is limited to targeted spot checks.

rejected_leads.lead: HttpServerExchange.getHostAndPort() applies the HTTP default-port check to HTTPS with port 8080 instead of 443 (core/src/main/java/io/undertow/server/HttpServerExchange.java:584-595), inconsistent with getHostPort() which correctly returns 443.
rejected_leads.reason: Only affects URL formatting in the fallback used when the Host header is absent (non-standard for HTTP/1.1); redirects may omit an explicit port but no attacker-controlled data is involved and no concrete security impact could be established. Possibly an upstream typo rather than a security defect.

rejected_leads.lead: Directory listing HTML is built without HTML-escaping the request path or file names (core/.../resource/DirectoryUtils.renderDirectoryListing lines 52-104, used by ResourceHandler and DefaultServlet).
rejected_leads.reason: Requires directory listing to be explicitly enabled and attacker-controlled file/directory names on the server filesystem; the rendered request path would additionally have to resolve to an existing directory, so a concrete reflected-XSS vector could not be demonstrated from source.

rejected_leads.lead: RedirectBuilder.realEncode appears to drop the character immediately before a '/' when re-encoding a path segment (core/src/main/java/io/undertow/util/RedirectBuilder.java:116-139, substring(pos, i - 1)).
rejected_leads.reason: Functional corruption of generated Location URLs; no attacker-controlled trust boundary or privilege impact identified, and it may be a long-standing upstream quirk.

rejected_leads.lead: Header values are not validated for CR/LF in HeaderMap/HeaderValues or in the response writer, so applications that place user input into headers could suffer response splitting (CWE-113).
rejected_leads.reason: No default handler or built-in flow reflects request-controlled data into a response header was found; exploitation requires application code, so the source evidence for a repository-level vulnerability is insufficient compared with the path-traversal candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: No automatic session-ID rotation on authentication (FormAuthenticationMechanism/SecurityContextImpl.login do not call changeSessionId), a possible session-fixation weakness.
rejected_leads.reason: Servlet 3.1 requires applications to call HttpServletRequest.changeSessionId(); no concrete exploit path and no repository-level enforcement failure could be proven from source.

rejected_leads.lead: Digest authentication has unimplemented QOP/auth-int handling and TODO comments about replay/validation ordering (core/.../security/impl/DigestAuthenticationMechanism.java).
rejected_leads.reason: The behaviors are clearly marked incomplete/TODO and are not enabled by default configurations inspected; no concrete auth-bypass flow could be traced.

summary: Repository: Undertow 1.0.16.Final (JBoss/Red Hat Java web server; modules core, servlet, websockets-jsr, examples, parser-generator). I inspected the HTTP request pipeline, servlet mapping/security handlers, resource serving, security mechanisms, session handling and representative WebSocket code, and used the P1 index to confirm key call edges (e.g., ServletSecurityConstraintHandler.handleRequest -> SecurityPathMatches.getSecurityInfo with exchange.getRelativePath()). The strongest source-evidenced issue is a missing path-canonicalization step for untrusted request paths before servlet routing, authorization-constraint evaluation and file-resource resolution. Because the HTTP parser only URL-decodes and never normalizes "." / ".." segments, and because the servlet container and resource managers consume that raw string, an unauthenticated client can reach resources that the reserved-directory checks (ServletInitialHandler.isForbiddenPath, DefaultServlet.isAllowed) and path-based security constraints are meant to protect (CWE-22, with a CWE-863 bypass flavor). I found no confirmed evidence for a stronger distinct issue (e.g., SQLi/command injection/deserialization/CRLF reflection by default are absent or require app-level flows), so only this one candidate is submitted.
